author: FX.Sniffer
text:
Hi Hotochin,

True.....conventional S/D trading suggests buying/selling from zone to zone at the first return back and if there are liquidity gaps on the left it will get filled in the process. However, a break through key levels or S/R and a close above or below helps to identify the shift in decision and the creation of a new decision point, and if this happens then the liquidity gaps will not get filled anytime soon and it's a sign of a strong trend depending on the time frame.

author: FX.Sniffer
text:
3D VS. 3T

There is a difference between the 3 Drives and the 3 Touch aka 3 Taps, both are a result of distribution and accumulation.

3D falls under the compression category and is a reversal move.

3T falls under the trend following category and is a continuation move, but also could a compression when price returns to it and breaks the 3rd touch.

The below image explain the difference and the 3D has been explained by IF
 here
. As for the 3T its simply a 3 touch of a trend-line.

In below image and on the left side is an example of a 3T into a down trend-line and the third touch was preceded by a lower low and formed a lower high, on the right side a 3T into an up trend-line and the third touch was preceded by a higher high then formed a higher low.

In IF's example you can see both patterns in his chart, a 3T followed by a 3D. For more on trend direction and the role of highs and lows refer to the
 Trend Direction / Highs and Lows Article
.

author: FX.Sniffer
text:
I’ve received an important pm that better be answered here, here is a part of it:

“Now before I met you guys here at RTM this year my view of what I can make in forex was different. I was considering 40% annual a good return. Now when my friend and I see your returns (yours, and others so on...) it's hard to believe this is possible. My friend looks at statistics and says that none of you guys are in Forbes 500 but with this % return all of you should be in there. Also claims that none of world best traders could average over 100% yearly. Well you get the point.

Now my friend has the point I agree, but also I spend days here and I see what you do and how. Well to make this shorter could you maybe shed some light for me?”

Now my feedback, I know why I’m not in Forbes. However, I had the same question regarding other traders (not necessarily in RTM) who shows their amazing consistent winners and makes you think that it’s so easy, and the issue that they don’t explain the reasons behind their entries and they never show you the bad trades. Some might learn something from their charts and others might not but in the end they could mislead you into a disaster. The internet is a double edged sword, anyone can post anything wether its false charts or demo results. Here in RTM we tried to avoid this by digging deep into the price action and teaching the reasons behind our entries and what is expected next, and we wish from whoever learns from our posts to carry on the torch and pass it over to new members.

So if you want my advice whatever results you see on the internet by others doesn’t mean anything, all you need is a method or to learn how to read the price and your results depends on you and your circumstances, if someone is showing unbelievable results it’s not necessarily fake or even true, and it doesn’t mean that you could achieve the same because by end of the day it all comes back to a certain factors.

1) Your personality & your circumstances: in short you can call it “psychology”, human behavior is common and the proof is if you meet a group of traders and share your trading stories you’ll find that you all share a lot in common, the same mistakes, fears, greed etc. and only the elite who succeed in this business are the ones who succeed in controlling their feelings and bend the circumstances to their advantage. Each trader has different circumstances that could either help or add pressure, for example are you trading part time or full time and do you have enough savings or do you need every cent you can make from the market, does your family/GF/BF supports you or not and so on.

2) Your startup capital: the amount of money in your balance plays a big role, the bigger accounts the better, of course rules are made to be broken and a trader can make thousands out of a hundred but also there are traders who wasted millions.

3) Your money/risk management: this one is much related to 1 & 2 as a cause & effect. MM could vary depending on capital and the personality, bigger capital allows you to use bigger contracts and bad MM could demolish big accounts, solid MM ease psychological pressure and bad psychology destroy all MM rules, the examples are endless.

4) Market state or condition: in some market conditions you can make huge profits, in others you can’t make a clear decision. For example if we consider you’re implementing a solid MM plan trading one instrument and everything is perfect the monthly ROI will never ever have the same result for the 12 month.

In fact all the above mentioned points are related and connected to each other as affects & effects.

So back to the Forbes list, I’ve never posted consistent profitable trades neither here nor anywhere else and never claimed that I achieve a certain monthly ROI, so this question is irrelevant to me but it could be asked to others if they claim or show such results. As for the yearly return % in general it depends on all the above points. In some of the live competitions traders have achieved more than a 100% ROI in one month, as for institutions, banks, hedge funds, regulated managed accounts etc their risk profiles are monitored & controlled by regulations so as their returns. Moreover, not all private independent traders show off or publish their ROI. Therefore, if you find anyone on the internet or anywhere else publishing their results without teaching then either they are scammers or showing off or looking for investors or selling something.

Here in RTM we had an objective to teach and maybe someday become a physical academy or even startup a fund management, this is why most of our posts are showing the why and how before or after and not just after the facts results.

So in short take the trading methods as it is or tweak it and ignore others results, don’t think about it, in the end your returns depends on YOU. I don’t guarantee that you’ll make a 100% yearly ROI or less or more because I don’t know you or your circumstances but I guarantee that you’ll save a lot of time in your journey.

Cheers,

author: Hotochin
text:
The first is the daily chart. The only main point here is to see the very important level that price was coming into. Price generally either flagged above or below this line.

The second chart is the 30min. Basically you have price come into the green line and FO by the pin bar. As Pedini has said the FO really fuels the move in the opposite direction. After the FO price engulfs the green ellipse and gives clues that it wants to go up farther. Your entry is by the return to the source of the engulf marked with a purple line.

The last chart is your 1min. I would bet that you went long when price returned to the green rectangle as price had already gone up and taken out supply.

H
